# 0012 — Documentation site generated by `hecate.doc` with an MDN-like theme

- **Status:** Proposed (owner preference recorded; spike OQ-11 validates feasibility)
- **Date:** 2026-10-11
- **Packages:** doc, website, cli
- **Related:** [documentation.md](../architecture/documentation.md), OQ-11 (spike pending: the owner decides on its report)

## Context

Documentation must be a separate site, exhaustive, easy to read and translated into
several languages. The owner's reference for look and readability is Lua Web Docs
(<https://luadocs.com>): MDN-style pages, guides, reference and runnable examples.
The owner prefers that Hecate generate its documentation with exactly that kind of
presentation, either by adapting an existing generator or by building one as a Hecate
module, so that the framework site and the documentation of user projects
(`hecate doc build`) share the same look.

## Options considered

1. **Adapt an existing generator**: VitePress or Astro Starlight with a custom MDN-like
   theme; LDoc with custom templates (reference only); the Lua Web Docs stack (Next.js
   with MDX).
2. **`hecate.doc` as a complete static site generator** (owner preference): guides
   in Markdown, reference from LuaLS annotations, API reference from OpenAPI, one
   MDN-like theme, locales, search index, versioning, runnable examples where possible.

## Decision (proposed)

Option 2, unless the OQ-11 spike shows it is unreasonable for the timeline, in which
case option 1 with a theme reproducing the same presentation.

- Content is written in Markdown with front matter, independent of the generator, so
  pages can be drafted before `hecate.doc` exists and survive a change of generator.
- The theme is Hecate's own. Lua Web Docs is an inspiration for structure and
  readability only (see "Licence finding" below).
- The same generator and theme serve the framework website and user projects.

### Owner direction, 2026-10-13: route 2, VitePress-like features, Hecate brand kit

Given by the project owner in chat; the OQ-11 report is still formally pending and **this
ADR keeps its status** (only the owner promotes ADRs). Until then it is the working
hypothesis:

- Route 2: `hecate.doc` is our own static site generator, written in Lua 5.5, with no
  third-party dependency (Markdown renderer, search index and theme scripts are written in
  the package; a dependency that seems needed is recorded as an open question, not added).
  *Superseded the same day by decision 4 below: dependencies are wanted where they save
  time.*
- The owner finds Starlight's look unattractive and prefers VitePress-like presentation:
  top navigation bar with logo, section links, search box, locale switch, theme toggle and
  GitHub link; left sidebar; right-hand "On this page" outline; previous/next cards at the
  bottom of pages; edit-this-page link; last updated; callout containers (note, tip,
  warning, danger); code blocks with a copy button and a language label; responsive mobile
  menu.
- The theme is original (no Tailwind UI code, no Lua Web Docs code) and strictly follows the
  Hecate brand kit: logo lockups and the compact mark for the favicon, light and dark
  tokens, STIX Two / Fira Sans / Fira Code, nearly square corners, no gradients or glows,
  the name never capitalised, earth (verdigris) as the single accent, WCAG 2.2 AA,
  keyboard navigation. Third-party material it vendors (fonts, brand files, one icon) is
  listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`.

First slice: `packages/doc` (see its README); choices left open are OQ-33 to OQ-38.

### Owner decisions on the OQ-11 questions, 2026-10-13

Given by the project owner in chat; **this ADR keeps its status** (only the owner promotes
ADRs). The seven answers below close the questions of the OQ-11 report. Where they differ
from the direction above, they prevail: in particular, "no third-party dependency" is
replaced by decision 4.

1. **Route (a):** `hecate.doc` generates everything (framework site and user projects).
   Nothing is planned on top of `hecate.template` for it: not in the near future.
2. **Timeline:** the earlier the documentation ships, the better. A minimal `hecate.doc`
   and the reference generator are pulled forward from Phase 3 (roadmap updated). A
   dependency of `doc` on `json` and `reactor` is accepted.
3. **Visual identity:** everything comes from the brand kit (`brand/` of the organisation
   `.github` repository); agents may read it.
4. **Third-party dependencies:** do not code from scratch where a Lua, C or Rust dependency
   saves time. Wanted: complete GitHub Flavoured Markdown; syntax highlighting for many
   languages through a dependency (no own lexers); OpenAPI reference rendering with no new
   JavaScript development tool (a Lua, C or Rust dependency if one exists, otherwise own
   rendering of the OpenAPI document into static pages). Each dependency still needs an
   ADR: see the spike [OQ-39](../spikes/OQ-39-doc-dependencies.md) and ADR 0022.
5. **WebAssembly:** as much as possible, provided the site stays deployable as static
   GitHub Pages files.
6. **Content conventions (agent's choice, recorded in
   [documentation.md](../architecture/documentation.md), OQ-35):** the page title is the
   single `#` heading of the body; front matter `title` is an optional override for
   navigation and `<title>`; code samples are included from tested files from the start.
7. **Reference generation:** every module table is annotated as a `---@class`, so the
   LuaLS export contains its functions; no annotation parser is written; parameters and
   returns are described with the standard `---@param name type description`.

## Licence finding (2026-10-11)

The owner wished to reproduce the exact theme of Lua Web Docs. That project is
distributed under the **Tailwind UI licence** (Tailwind Labs Inc.), which:

- is granted only to the purchaser (one individual, or up to 25 employees and
  contractors of a business), so it does not extend to Hecate through Lua Web Docs;
- forbids redistributing the components and templates or their derivatives separately
  from an end product, and creating a theme, template or starter kit from them;
- forbids end products designed to let end users build their own end products with
  them ("website builder").

Consequently the theme **cannot be embedded in `hecate.doc`**, because `hecate.doc`
generates documentation sites for users. At most, the public Hecate website alone could
use a Tailwind UI template under a licence purchased by the owner. This reading is not
legal advice; Tailwind Labs answers licence questions at <support@tailwindui.com>.

### Owner decision on the theme (2026-10-11)

**An original Hecate theme everywhere** (framework website and user projects), rejecting
both a Tailwind UI template for the public site only and a request for permission to
Tailwind Labs. The theme:

- reproduces the *qualities* of MDN and Lua Web Docs (clear navigation, fixed reference
  page template, readable typography, runnable examples), not their code or visual
  assets;
- is written for Hecate and released under the MIT licence inside `packages/doc`;
- may use open-source tooling under compatible licences (for example the MIT-licensed
  Tailwind CSS framework, which is distinct from the restricted Tailwind UI
  components), recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`;
- supports light and dark modes, keyboard navigation and WCAG 2.2 AA contrast;
- has its visual identity (colours, logo, typography) validated by the owner on
  rendered samples during the OQ-11 spike.

The remaining open point of this ADR is the generator route (option 1 or 2), decided on
the OQ-11 report.

## Consequences

- Dogfooding: `hecate.doc` becomes a substantial package (Markdown rendering, templating,
  search index, i18n). It may anticipate parts of `hecate.template`.
- The public website appears later than with an off-the-shelf generator; an interim
  plain rendering of the Markdown pages is acceptable until then.

## Verification

Website build in CI with `hecate doc`; broken-link check; translation-status report;
visual review of rendered samples by the owner during the spike.
